newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion closes down on global setbacks.
newsitem.headline: India bullion closes down on global setbacks.

text.p: Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees lower at 4,480 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,515 rupees as losses in the world market triggered fresh selling, dealer said.
Gold was down by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Tuesday.
"Sluggish seasonal demand and fears the Indian government may further liberalise import policy for gold also subdued market sentiment," said M.L. Damani, president of Bombay Bullion Exchange.

Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) closed 400 rupees lower at 52,400 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Tuesday. Premiums of import licences for bullion however rose from 13.10 percent to 13.25 percent.

Silver (.999) closed 105 rupees lower at 6,325 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,430 rupees following unloading by local stockists after sharp losses in the world market. Silver was up by 30 rupees per kg on Tuesday.

"Local silver prices actually opened 105 rupees per kg lower in early trade but expectation of the seasonal buying at the lower level arrested further fall in the prices during the day," said Mahavir Shah, a leading dealer.
